newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela asks US to help deepen Maracaibo channel. [CORRECTED 00:28 GMT 17/04]
newsitem.headline: Venezuela asks US to help deepen Maracaibo channel. [CORRECTED 00:28 GMT 17/04]

text.p: Venezuela's government said it will ask the U.S. to help deepen Lake Maracaibo's navigation channel -- site of three recent tanker groundings and through which some 70 percent of Venezuela's oil exports pass.
"There has to be an investigation, and I've asked the US embassy to help," Transport Minister Moises Orozco told reporters.

As the channel was built by the U.S. army in 1928, and subsequently deepened by them in 1950, Orozco did not blame (corrects to remove the blame from the pilots) Maracaibo pilots who guide tankers out to sea for the three groundings.
"However, it's very possible that the channel is no longer large enough for today's tankers," he said.
The pilots have threatened to go on strike Monday if demands to limit shipping to tankers with a 36 feet draught, from the current 38 feet limit, are not met.
Pilots representative Fidel Sanchez said the channel was clogged with sediment and that the groundings "are clearly the fault of the National Channel Institute".
Pilots, Ministry and Institute representatives are due to meet Thursday to discuss the channel and the pilots' demands.
